proposal.claim:
Origin, stated before anything else. This proposal is NOT from reports/SCOUT.jsonl, and the reason is a property of the evaluator rather than of the notebook. The notebook holds six payers and not one is reachable with the fields this project can express. Four are anchored to a calendar or to an announcement -- the quarterly delivery fixing averaged over the 07:00-08:00 UTC hour of the last Friday of a quarter; the pre-announced margin-tier tightening on one named symbol at one stated minute; the BUSD/USDC collateral wind-down; the delisting settlement at an index average on the venue's own date -- and neither TrialConfig nor SignalTrialConfig has any field that can name a date, an hour of day, a weekday, or an announcement. A Track A programme is anchored only to its own start offset and the evaluator enumerates EVERY start offset, so a calendar cohort cannot even be isolated inside the ensemble, let alone gated on; a 5th-percentile statistic taken across all offsets averages the fixing hour away by construction. The two remaining payers -- the liquidated short forced to cover, and the short-gamma dealer hedging into an expiry -- both need an intrabar forced-flow proxy, and this project has now spent two proposals (H0008's generic take-profit, H0009's trailing-peak gate) discovering that no such proxy exists in its vocabulary. The delisting payer carries a second, independent blocker: it is an alt-basket claim and KT-3 is inconclusive. So the notebook is unreachable, this proposal says so rather than borrowing an unreachable payer's language for a reachable rule, and that borrowing is precisely what killed H0008.

What is left, and it is one thing. Track A's expressible vocabulary is a deposit schedule, a gate, two terminating exits, leverage, a funding switch and cost knobs. Gates are H0007's shape and H0009 was killed for returning to them under a new threshold. Leverage above 1x is KT-2, closed. The cost knobs are robustness's job and cost zero ledger rows there. That leaves the schedule geometry and the exits -- which means the only structural transfer Track A can express at all is the one KT-1 already measured: the rent a perpetual charges its holder, per hour, on notional. This hypothesis sits on the paying side of that transfer and does not pretend otherwise.

Who is structurally paying, and why they keep doing it. We are, and the receiver is whoever stands short the perpetual against inventory -- the carry side, flat on price and long the coupon. They keep collecting because the leveraged long keeps standing there to be charged: KT-1 measured 87% of BTCUSDT settlements positive and a median bill of 36% of contributed capital over a three-year weekly ladder. The reason that number is 87% and not 50% is that the perpetual is how a leveraged directional view is expressed on this venue, and a long who waits for the rate to normalise has missed the move he is paying to be in. That is a property of the product, not of one regime.

Why the SHAPE decides the size of that bill, and what has never been asked. The rent is charged on NOTIONAL HELD PER HOUR. It is not charged on capital contributed. Two accumulation programmes that run for exactly the same number of days, with the same per-deposit size and the same weekly frequency, therefore owe materially different bills purely because of WHEN their notional arrives. Deposit for 13 weeks and then hold for 1001 days, and the book stands at roughly 0.958 of a fully deployed one measured in notional-hours over the horizon; deposit for 78 weeks and hold for 546 days and it stands at roughly 0.750. That is a 28% difference in rent for an identical horizon and an identical schedule frequency. Track A has never tested this because its grid could not: H0001's horizon IS stride_days x n_contributions, so every change to the deposit count moved the holding time with it. H0001's own surface reading concludes that 'the metric responds only to the product' -- which is a claim that deployment speed does not matter, asserted from a grid in which deployment speed could not be varied independently of the horizon. This grid holds the horizon constant along a diagonal and varies the deployment speed along it, which is the comparison the equity-market question (lump sum against drip) is normally decided on and which no Track A family has ever run.

The design. contribution is fixed at 100 and stride_days at 7, and the grid crosses n_contributions [13, 39, 78] with hold_days [546, 819, 1001]. Three cells share a total programme length of exactly 1092 days -- (13, 1001), (39, 819), (78, 546) -- which is KT-1's three-year frame, so the funding fraction these cells report is directly comparable with the 36% KT-1 measured on the same frame. None of the three deposit counts is a value H0001 enumerated (it used 52, 104, 156), and none of these cells exists anywhere in its grid, because H0001 held hold_days at zero. Along the diagonal the total money contributed differs (1300, 3900 and 7800 USD), so the comparison is made on the money-weighted RATE, which is invariant to how much money a programme moves; tm_q05 is reported beside it as section 4 requires and, because the three diagonal cells share one horizon, tm_q05 is for once legitimately comparable between them and PBO is computable -- H0001's 'fewer than two configurations share a horizon' is designed out here rather than rediscovered. include_funding is on the grid because it is the only attribution this vocabulary offers: with the rent switched off, the three diagonal cells differ only by drift and by averaging, so the difference between the two orderings IS the rent's contribution to the ranking. The universe is chosen two against two across the funding sign: BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT net PAY funding over this window, SOLUSDT and BNBUSDT net RECEIVED it (H0007's surface reading records those two flipping the sign of include_funding). If the mechanism is the rent, the effect has to change direction across that split.

What is honestly weak. Four symbols, and Track A's independence comes from start dates over a single history: H0001 reports between 1.02 and 1.40 independent paths per symbol on comparable horizons, so a 1092-day cell is close to ONE experiment per symbol and the diagonal is at best four experiments. The corner cell (78, 1001) runs 1547 days and is expected to return NaN on SOLUSDT and BNBUSDT and possibly on ETHUSDT; those are unmeasured cells, not results. And nothing in this shape can pay the accumulator. The best available outcome is a geometry that pays less rent, which is a map entry and not an edge, and the report must not describe it as one.
proposal.kill_condition:
Let I(n, h, f) be the annualised money-weighted return at the 5th percentile of start dates (mwrr_q05) for n_contributions n, hold_days h and include_funding f. The three constant-horizon cells are D1 = (13, 1001), D2 = (39, 819) and D3 = (78, 546), each a total programme length of 1092 days. Let R(n, h) = I(n, h, false) - I(n, h, true), the annualised rent the shape paid.

Closed if deployment speed does not move the left tail at a fixed horizon: if max I(D, true) - min I(D, true) over the three diagonal cells is below 0.02 -- two annualised percentage points -- on 3 or more of the 4 symbols. The geometry then has no effect the metric can see and there is nothing to map.

Closed also, even if that bar is cleared, if the effect is not the rent: if the rank order of I over D1, D2, D3 is identical with include_funding true and with include_funding false on 3 or more of the 4 symbols. The ordering is then produced by drift and averaging on a book that pays nothing, it would exist on spot, and it belongs to no perpetual-specific mechanism this family named.

Closed also if the rent is not shape-dependent in the predicted direction: if the absolute value of R is not strictly decreasing across D1 -> D2 -> D3 on 3 or more of the 4 symbols. Notional-hours over the fixed 1092 days stand at approximately 0.958, 0.875 and 0.750 of a fully deployed book for D1, D2 and D3, so a charge levied on notional per hour must fall in that order whatever its sign. If it does not, the bill is not being charged the way this family assumes and no clause above may be read as a mechanism.

Closed as unmeasurable, rather than false, if the funding split does not appear: if sign(R(D1)) is the same on all four symbols. The universe was chosen two paying against two receiving precisely so that the direction of the transfer must differ across it; one sign everywhere means either that the split assumption taken from H0007's surface is wrong on this frame or that the switch is not measuring who paid whom, and in either case the attribution clause above is not interpretable.

Closed also if the best diagonal cell's shape diagnostic reads SPIKE on 3 or more of the 4 symbols. Both grid axes carry three numeric levels, so every diagonal cell has a neighbour on each side in both n_contributions and hold_days and this clause is computable; the two-level grid that made the identical clause unrunnable in H0006 is deliberately not repeated.

Closed also if the reported PBO is at or above 0.5 on a majority of the symbols for which it is computed. The three diagonal cells share one horizon by construction, so this clause is expected to be evaluable; if PBO comes back uncomputed on all four symbols, the report must record that this family's selection was never tested rather than counting this clause as survived.

Not counted toward any clause above: any cell whose total programme length 7n + hold_days exceeds a symbol's pre-seal history returns NaN. (78, 1001) is 1547 days and is expected to be NaN on SOLUSDT and BNBUSDT and possibly ETHUSDT. Such cells are unmeasured, not results.

verdict.reason: [claude] The proposal asserts "nothing here terminates early" at leverage 1.0, but funding-driven liquidation does: on the very cells its kill condition names I measure liquidation_rate 0.430 on DOGEUSDT and 0.190 on ETHUSDT, which floors tm_q05 and makes G a distance-to-ruin measure rather than a bill — clause 1 then evaluates to 2.66x/2.54x/1.24x/0.37x (BTC/ETH/BNB/DOGE), fires on "at least 3 of the 4", and would permanently close a mechanism that funding_frac_q50 on the funded arm alone shows at 4.91x/4.91x/1.81x. That same metric, funding_paid/invested, is already profiled per start date on every funded row, so the include_funding axis spends 36 of the 72 configurations reconstructing by tail-differenced subtraction a quantity the runner records exactly and for free — the notional-time question is answerable today by a script with zero ledger rows. | [codex] This is a finer grid over H0001’s unconditional DCA rule form—varying the existing hold_days and stride_days parameters—not a new rule shape; it also re-litigates the structural long-perpetual funding tax already closed by KT-1. The fixed-horizon comparison is well specified, but novelty in experimental contrast does not make a new mechanism family.
